title: Efficacy of preoperative transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation in reducing postoperative delirium in older adults undergoing orthopedic surgery: a randomized controlled trial.
uncertainty_reason: Mixed anaesthetic techniques were used and outcomes were not reported separately by general-anaesthesia subgroup.
general_anaesthesia: mixed; some participants received spinal anaesthesia
comparator: Visually identical modified device with no current on same schedule
evidence_summary: Randomized therapeutic TEAS trial with eligible clinical outcomes; retained because some patients clearly underwent GA, but mixed spinal/GA outcome separability is unresolved and was flagged for human review rather than used for exclusion.
notes: Sensitivity-first retention under the protocol; requires adjudication of mixed-anaesthesia eligibility.

title: Randomized Trial on Electroacupuncture for Recovery of Postoperative Gastrointestinal Function Based on Long-Term Monitoring Device.
uncertainty_reason: General anaesthesia was not explicitly stated and airway/anaesthetic technique was not described; laparoscopic radical gastrectomy strongly suggests GA but is not sufficient for definitive classification without human adjudication.
comparator: Same needle procedure and electrodes with no current
evidence_summary: Randomized adult operative EA trial with eligible timing, comparator and clinical GI outcomes; retained with human-review flag because the full text does not explicitly establish general anaesthesia.
notes: Sensitivity-first retention; NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW — anaesthesia type not explicitly reported.

title: A Randomized Controlled Trial Assessing the Impact of Transcutaneous Electrical Acupoint Stimulation on Gastrointestinal Motility, Nutritional Status, and Immune Function in Patients Following Cerebrovascular Accident Surgery.
uncertainty_reason: General anaesthesia was not explicitly reported, and TEAS timing was stated as within 24-48 h after cerebrovascular onset or before enteral feeding rather than relative to surgery; neither criterion could be definitively excluded.
comparator: Same acupoint electrodes and duration as sham TEAS plus identical nutritional/ICU care
evidence_summary: Randomized adult postoperative TEAS trial with separable sham comparison and eligible GI/ICU outcomes; retained with human-review flags because both GA and surgery-relative first-treatment timing remain unresolved.
notes: Sensitivity-first retention; NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW — anaesthesia type and surgery-relative timing unreported.

title: Effect of acupuncture on postoperative ileus after laparoscopic elective colorectal surgery: A prospective, randomised, controlled trial.
uncertainty_reason: The full report does not explicitly identify the anaesthetic technique; it excludes patients receiving epidural anaesthesia, but laparoscopic colorectal surgery alone is insufficient to establish general anaesthesia.
comparator: Standardized postoperative ERAS care without EA or other bowel-motility intervention
evidence_summary: Randomized adult postoperative EA trial with eligible surgery, stimulation, comparator and clinical outcomes; retained sensitivity-first with human-review flag because general anaesthesia is not positively established.
notes: NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW — anaesthesia type not explicitly reported; no inference made solely from laparoscopic colorectal surgery.

title: Electroacupuncture Improves Cerebral Vasospasm and Functional Outcome of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
uncertainty_reason: The report includes both endovascular coiling and surgical clipping but never states the anaesthetic technique or provides outcome data separable by anaesthesia type; general anaesthesia therefore cannot be established.
comparator: Standard medical treatment without EA; abstract describes mock transcutaneous stimulation but Methods states no EA treatment
evidence_summary: Randomized postoperative EA trial after operative aneurysm treatment with eligible stimulation, comparator and functional outcome; retained sensitivity-first with human-review flag because general anaesthesia and subgroup separability are not established.
notes: NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW — anaesthesia type not explicitly reported; no subgroup information invented.

title: Perioperative Electroacupuncture Can Accelerate the Recovery of Gastrointestinal Function in Cancer Patients Undergoing Pancreatectomy or Gastrectomy: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
uncertainty_reason: The complete full report does not explicitly state the anaesthetic technique or airway management; general anaesthesia cannot be inferred solely from pancreatectomy or gastrectomy.
comparator: Nonpenetrating blunt placebo needles with internally disconnected wire/no current on the same schedule
evidence_summary: Randomized adult cancer-surgery needle-EA trial with credible nonpenetrating/no-current sham and clinical gastrointestinal recovery outcomes; retained sensitivity-first with human-review flag because general anaesthesia is unreported.
notes: NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW — anaesthesia type not explicitly reported; no inference made solely from pancreatectomy/gastrectomy. #1920 had been fully reviewed as a possible final decision but was no longer present in the Covidence vote-required queue, so no decision was cast for it.
